## TL;DR

Added a touch gesture path for the Board and Pipeline card activity recency tooltip. The path is explicitly opted in with `data-touch-tip`, and only the recency status triggers receive that attribute. A tap opens and pins the existing styled tooltip while suppressing the trigger’s click; holding for 500 ms opens it as well. A canceled touch clears its pending gesture and cannot open the tooltip. Touching a different tooltip host dismisses the pinned tooltip while allowing that host’s click to continue. The required scoped RepoOS check passed on the final implementation tree.

## Work and rationale

The task asks that touch support be limited to the last-activity popover. I first read the task file and reviews 2 through 8 from #1058. Those reviews document three recurring failures: suppressing clicks for all tooltip hosts broke unrelated controls, `pointercancel` was incorrectly treated as a successful release, and switching to another tooltip host consumed its click. I also searched the work files for an active mobile rewrite. No such task or replacement implementation is present in this branch, and `lib/tooltip.ts` remains the delegated shared tooltip used by cards and the rest of the application. The narrow change therefore belongs in this task.

In `lib/tooltip.ts`, touch handling now recognizes only elements marked with `data-touch-tip`. Touch `pointerdown` dismisses any currently visible tooltip. If the target is opted in and has tooltip text, it arms a 500 ms long-press timer. A successful release on that same trigger opens the tooltip immediately for a tap, or leaves the long-press tooltip open. The next click is canceled only when it came from the exact opted-in trigger that started the gesture; the guard clears after one click. A different, non-opted-in tooltip host does not inherit that suppression, so its ordinary click handler still runs. `pointercancel` clears the timer and gesture state and hides the tooltip.

The Board status hint and Board check-progress trigger opt in only while they have activity recency text. Pipeline status and check-progress triggers do the same while their elapsed/activity tooltip is available. This preserves a single source of tooltip copy and leaves all other `title` and `data-tip` hosts on their existing mouse and keyboard behavior.

Added gesture regression tests in the existing card activity suite. They verify a tap opens the tooltip and suppresses its own click, a 500 ms long press opens and suppresses its click, cancellation before the threshold does not open it, and starting a touch on another tooltip host dismisses the pinned tooltip without consuming that host’s click. Existing board and pipeline assertions continue to cover the recency copy and trigger availability.

## Approaches tried

I considered whether this should wait for a broader mobile rewrite, as the task notes suggest. A work-file search found no mobile rewrite task in this branch, and the shared tooltip remains in active use across many controls. Replacing or globally altering that mechanism would recreate the scope problem reported in #1058. I kept the implementation delegated and added an explicit per-trigger attribute instead.

I also kept the tooltip’s existing content and placement logic. The new gesture path calls the same `show` routine used by hover/focus so the touch state presents the identical popover. The only gesture-specific state is the active opted-in target, long-press timer, whether that timer opened the tooltip, and the one-shot click target.

## Challenges and blockers

The shared tooltip is attached at the document level, so touch event ordering matters: pointer capture handlers run before card click handlers. The implementation uses that ordering only for an opted-in recency trigger and does not stop propagation on pointer events. Click suppression is deferred to the ensuing click and matched against the gesture’s original target. This addresses the earlier failure where dismissing one pinned tooltip also swallowed the next control’s action.

The implementation was verified through automated tests, a production build, rendered contrast audit, and UI smoke test. No real phone or tablet interaction was performed, so this report does not claim physical-device verification. The timing threshold is 500 ms and may merit a human feel check on a touch device.

## Key learnings

The prior review history was useful as a regression map: the main risk was not drawing the tooltip, but deciding which gestures are allowed to cancel which clicks. Keeping the opt-in marker on only the recency triggers makes that boundary visible in the components and testable at the document listener.

A second useful constraint is to model cancellation separately from release. A pointer cancellation must tear down pending state and must never be routed through the successful tap/long-press path. Likewise, click suppression should be one-shot and bound to the exact opted-in trigger rather than represented as a global “touch tooltip active” condition.

Validation: `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed on the final code and test tree. Remote validation built the app and passed 404 tests across 36 changed-path files, followed by browser gates. Local format, lint, build, CSS and theme guards, rendered contrast audit, and UI smoke also passed.
